examples.en: My uncle emigrated to Canada.
My family is emigrating to Australia next year.

examples.ko: 이민하는 사람은 먼저 비자를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: People who emigrate must get a visa first.
I haven't chosen the country to emigrate to yet.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때 부모님과 이민해서 영어를 잘해요.
examples.en: He emigrated with his parents as a child, so he speaks English well.

examples.ko: 이민하고 나서 처음 몇 달이 가장 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The first few months after emigrating were the hardest.

explain: 말할 때는 '이민 가다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '이민하다'는 글이나 설명에서 보이고, '미국으로 이민하다'처럼 '으로/로'와 써요. 일이나 공부 때문에 잠깐 가는 것은 이민이 아니에요. 들어오는 쪽은 '이민 오다'예요.

phrases.en: My friend emigrated to Australia.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 표현이고, 다른 나라로 살러 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most natural spoken form, used for moving to live in another country.

phrases.example: 저는 십 년 전에 한국에 이민 왔어요.
phrases.en: I immigrated to Korea ten years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이민 가다'와 반대로, 들어오는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 이민 가다; it is said from the side of the country people move into.

phrases.en: I want to emigrate to Canada someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바라는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -고 싶다 to talk about something you want to do.

explain_en: In speech, '이민 가다' sounds much more natural. '이민하다' shows up in writing and explanations, and takes 으로/로, as in '미국으로 이민하다'. Going abroad briefly for work or study is not 이민. Coming in from abroad is '이민 오다'.

examples.en: I found a small place to rent near the university.

examples.ko: 자취방이 좁아서 책상을 놓을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: My room is small, so there's no space for a desk.
My friends came over to my place.

examples.ko: 자취방 월세가 한 달에 오십만 원이에요.
examples.en: The monthly rent for my room is 500,000 won.
I cooked and ate ramyeon in my room.
A rented room is good when it gets plenty of sunlight.

explain: '자취하다'는 밥과 빨래를 직접 하며 혼자 사는 거예요. 밥을 챙겨 주는 '하숙'과 달라요. 건물 형태로는 '원룸'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a rented room near school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살 방을 찾을 때 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation for finding a room to live in.

phrases.en: I live in a small rented room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에 산다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where you live.

phrases.en: It's a studio, so there's only one room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 형태로 부르는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that names the type of housing.

explain_en: '자취하다' means living alone and doing your own cooking and laundry. It differs from '하숙', where meals are provided. By building type it can also be called a '원룸'.

t90.ax: My friends came over to my place.

examples.en: This temple was built a thousand years ago.
It is a city with a thousand years of history.
They say that tree has lived for a thousand years.

examples.ko: 천년이 지나도 이 노래는 기억될 거예요.
examples.en: Even after a thousand years, this song will be remembered.
It's special because it's a tradition that has lasted a thousand years.

examples.ko: 천년 전 사람들도 별을 보며 길을 찾았어요.
examples.en: People a thousand years ago also found their way by looking at the stars.

explain: 맞춤법으로는 '천 년'처럼 띄어 쓰는 경우가 많고, '수천 년'은 '몇천 년'의 뜻으로 써요. 정확히 1000년이라기보다 '아주 오랜 시간'을 말할 때도 많아요. 비슷한 말로 '오랜 세월'이 있어요.

phrases.en: Let's live together forever.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정말 오랫동안이라는 뜻으로 과장해서 말할 때 써요. 보통 '살다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration meaning for a very, very long time. It usually appears with verbs like '살다' (to live).

explain_en: In standard spelling it is often written with a space, '천 년', and '수천 년' means several thousand years. It is often used for 'a very long time' rather than exactly 1,000 years. A similar expression is '오랜 세월' (long years).

examples.en: My older sister gave birth to a healthy baby at the hospital.
My sister-in-law is giving birth next month.
She's resting at home after giving birth.
Her husband was beside her on the day she gave birth.
To give birth, you need to choose a hospital in advance.

examples.ko: 출산할 때 필요한 물건을 미리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought the things I need for the birth in advance.

explain: '출산하다'는 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 병원 안내에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '아기를 낳다'가 더 자연스러워요. 명사로 '출산 휴가', '출산율', '출산 준비'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My cousin gave birth to a baby last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출산하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in everyday conversation than the formal headword.
phrases.en_equiv: to give birth to a baby

phrases.example: 회사에서 출산 휴가를 석 달 받았어요.
phrases.en: I got three months of maternity leave from my company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 낳은 사람이 일을 쉬는 휴가를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to leave from work for giving birth.

phrases.example: 올케가 출산 준비로 아기 옷을 샀어요.
phrases.en: My sister-in-law bought baby clothes to prepare for the birth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 낳기 전에 하는 준비를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the preparations made before a baby is born.

explain_en: '출산하다' is formal and appears in the news and hospital notices. In everyday talk, '아기를 낳다' is more natural. The noun is common in '출산 휴가' (maternity leave), '출산율' (birth rate) and '출산 준비' (birth preparation).

t90.ax: She's resting at home after giving birth.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a fencer.
I watched a fencing match at the Olympics.
In fencing, quick footwork is important.
I am learning fencing at school.
The Korean fencing team won a gold medal.

examples.ko: 펜싱 마스크를 쓰면 얼굴이 안 보여요.
examples.en: When you wear a fencing mask, your face is not visible.

explain: 펜싱은 칼로 점수를 겨루는 운동이에요. 에페, 플뢰레, 사브르 세 종목이 있어요. '펜싱을 하다'처럼 말하고, 탁구나 테니스는 '치다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I do fencing every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이름 뒤에 '하다'를 붙여 그 운동을 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 하다 after the sport name to say you do or play that sport.

phrases.en: A fencing competition will be held next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 펜싱 경기가 열리는 행사를 말할 때 '펜싱' 뒤에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it after 펜싱 to name an event where fencing matches are held.

phrases.en: I'm learning fencing at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 시작하거나 연습하는 중일 때 '배우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 배우다 when you are starting out or still practicing.

explain_en: Fencing is a sport where two people score points with swords. There are three events: epee, foil and sabre. You say '펜싱을 하다', while table tennis and tennis sometimes take '치다'.

examples.en: My grandfather played the harmonica for me.
This harmonica is small, so it fits in a pocket.
I tried playing an easy children's song on the harmonica.
I heard a harmonica sound and looked out the window.
I do not know where the harmonica went.
I want to learn both the harmonica and the guitar.

explain: 입으로 불어서 소리를 내므로 '하모니카를 불다'라고 해요. 악기마다 동사가 달라서 피아노와 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'라고 해요. '연주하다'는 모든 악기에 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I play the harmonica every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입으로 부는 악기라서 '불다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It's played by blowing, so '불다' is used.

phrases.en: The sound of the harmonica is really gentle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about the instrument's sound.

phrases.en: That singer plays the harmonica.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연주하다'는 모든 악기에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '연주하다' works for any instrument.

explain_en: You make the sound by blowing, so you say '하모니카를 불다'. The verb changes by instrument: '치다' for piano and guitar, '켜다' for violin. '연주하다' works for any instrument.

examples.en: We have lived in the same neighborhood since we were little.
He is a friend from my neighborhood, so we meet often.
We live in the same neighborhood, but I don't even know their name.
We aren't in the same neighborhood, but we live close.
We lived in the same neighborhood, so we went to school together.
The neighborhood people gathered and held a feast.

explain: '같은 동네'와 거의 같은 뜻인데, '한동네'는 가깝고 정이 있는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '한동네 친구', '한동네에 살다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: We live in the same neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '한동네'보다 정이 덜 느껴지고 더 평범해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but sounds plainer and less warm than 한동네.

phrases.en: He is from my neighborhood, so I know him well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까이 사는 이웃을 정답게 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warm way to call someone who lives nearby.

phrases.en: We grew up in the same neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어릴 때부터 가까이 지낸 사이를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for people close since childhood.
phrases.en_equiv: to grow up in the same neighborhood

explain_en: It means almost the same as '같은 동네', but '한동네' carries a feeling of closeness and warmth. It is usually used in phrases like '한동네 친구' or '한동네에 살다'.

en: to be active; to engage in activities

examples.en: I'm very active in a school club.
That singer is working in Japan.
I was active in a volunteer group for three years.
The weather these days is good for being outdoors and active.
There are many actors working in both films and dramas.

examples.ko: 아이들이 활동할 수 있는 공간이 필요해요.
examples.en: The kids need a space where they can be active.

explain: '일하다'는 직장에서 하는 일 전체를 두루 가리키고, '활동하다'는 동아리, 봉사, 연예계처럼 어떤 분야나 모임에서 움직일 때 어울려요. 가수나 배우가 어디서 일하는지 말할 때도 '활동하다'를 자주 써요. 명사 '활동'은 '동아리 활동', '봉사 활동'처럼 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: That actor is very active these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '활발하게'를 붙이면 많이 움직이고 일한다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 활발하게 stresses being very busy and active.

phrases.en: That singer started their career last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가수나 배우가 일을 처음 시작할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a singer or actor begins their career.

phrases.en: I am active in a volunteer club.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여서 지금 계속 하고 있다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 있다 says you are doing it on an ongoing basis.

explain_en: '일하다' covers working in general, while '활동하다' fits clubs, volunteering, or fields like entertainment. For singers and actors it tells where they work, as in '일본에서 활동해요'. The noun '활동' is even more common, in phrases like '동아리 활동' and '봉사 활동'.

t90.ax: That singer is working in Japan.

examples.en: I had a lot of things in my heart that I wanted to say.

examples.ko: 가슴속 울분을 글로 풀어내자 마음이 한결 가벼워졌어요.
examples.en: Once I let out the anger in my heart through writing, my mind felt much lighter.

examples.ko: 그 말을 가슴속 깊이 새겨 두었어요.
examples.en: I engraved those words deep in my heart.
It feels refreshing, as if my chest were wide open.

examples.ko: 가슴속에만 담아 두지 말고 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't keep it only inside your heart. Try talking about it.

examples.ko: 아버지의 마지막 말씀이 아직도 가슴속에 남아 있어요.
examples.en: My father's last words still remain in my heart.

explain: '마음속'과 비슷하지만 '가슴속'은 울분이나 그리움처럼 가슴이 답답하거나 벅찬 감정에 잘 어울려요. 생각이나 기억은 '머릿속'이라고 해요. 보통 '가슴속에', '가슴속 깊이'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I kept those words deep in my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이나 말을 아주 깊이 품고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you hold a feeling or words very deeply inside.

phrases.example: 그날의 일이 아직도 가슴속에 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: What happened that day still stays in my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잊히지 않는 감정이나 일이 오래 마음에 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a feeling or event stays with you and isn't forgotten.

phrases.en: I have a lot of worries on my mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가슴속'과 비슷하지만 '마음속'은 감정뿐 아니라 생각에도 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 가슴속, but 마음속 is broader and can be used for thoughts as well as feelings.

explain_en: It is similar to '마음속', but '가슴속' fits feelings that make the chest tight or full, like anger or longing. Thoughts and memories go in '머릿속'. It is usually used as '가슴속에' or '가슴속 깊이'.

examples.en: I resolved to exercise steadily this year.

examples.ko: 친구는 매일 책을 읽기로 결심해서 도서관 카드를 만들었어요.
examples.en: My friend resolved to read every day, so she made a library card.

examples.ko: 그는 한국에서 살기로 결심한 뒤에 한국어를 배웠어요.
examples.en: After he decided to live in Korea, he learned Korean.
I made up my mind to study abroad and sent my documents to the school.
Even if you resolve to, keeping it isn't easy.
Since it was a hard decision for you, I'll cheer you on too.

explain: '-기로 결심하다'처럼 앞으로 할 일을 굳게 정할 때 자주 써요. 선택지 중에서 하나를 고를 때는 '결정하다'를 쓰고, 가벼운 마음은 '마음먹다'가 더 입말이에요. '결심이 서다'처럼 명사로도 나와요.

phrases.en: I decided to learn English next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어를 해요체 과거로 말한 형태로, 이미 마음을 정했다고 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form, used to say you have already made up your mind.

phrases.en: I made up my mind to go to bed early from today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결심하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 가벼운 결정이고 입말에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '결심하다' but lighter and more common in speech.

phrases.en: I finally made up my mind to move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '결심'을 써서 마음이 굳게 정해졌다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '결심' to say that one's resolve has firmly formed.

explain_en: It is often used as '-기로 결심하다' when firmly settling on what you will do. Picking one of several options is '결정하다', and a lighter resolve is more casually '마음먹다'. It also appears as a noun in '결심이 서다'.

t90.ax: I resolved to exercise steadily this year.

examples.ko: 해외 주재원의 자녀 교육 문제는 늘 큰 고민거리예요.
examples.en: Educating children of overseas postings is always a big worry.

examples.ko: 요즘 고민거리가 많아서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I have a lot on my mind lately, so I can't sleep.
If you have something troubling you, tell me.
Getting a job was my biggest worry.
I told my friend what was bothering me and felt better.
The child's grades became a worry for the parents.

explain: '고민거리가 생기다/있다/되다'처럼 써요. '걱정거리'와 비슷한데, 고민거리는 어떻게 할지 생각이 많은 문제에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I have a lot of worries these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 걱정되는 마음에 더 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but focuses more on the feeling of being worried.

phrases.en: Moving has become a big worry for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 고민이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something turns into a concern.

phrases.en: I told my friend about my worries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속마음을 솔직하게 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for opening up about what's on your mind.

explain_en: It is used as '고민거리가 생기다/있다/되다'. It is close to '걱정거리', but '고민거리' fits problems where you keep thinking about what to do.

t90.ax: Getting a job was my biggest worry.

examples.en: I'm torn about which school to choose.
I kept agonizing over what to get as a gift.

examples.ko: 새 일을 시작할지 고민되는 마음을 이해해요.
examples.en: I understand the feeling of being torn about starting a new job.

examples.ko: 이사 문제가 고민돼서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The moving issue was weighing on me, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 둘 다 마음에 들어서 정말 고민되네요.
examples.en: I like both, so it's really hard to decide.
If you're too troubled, try talking to a friend.

explain: '고민하다'는 내가 오래 생각하는 행동이고, '고민되다'는 마음속에 망설임이 생기는 느낌이에요. 보통 '~ㄹ지 고민돼요'처럼 선택이 어려울 때 써요. 걱정만 있는 상황은 '걱정되다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I have many things to worry over these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로, 마음에 걸리는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun for things weighing on your mind.

phrases.en: When I'm torn about something, I ask my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 때'를 붙여 망설여지는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -(으)ㄹ 때 refers to the times when you feel torn.

phrases.example: 뭘 먹을지 고민돼서 메뉴를 오래 봤어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't decide what to eat, so I looked at the menu for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고민하는 이유를 뒤 문장과 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the worry as the reason for what follows.

explain_en: 고민하다 is the act of thinking something over for a long time, while 고민되다 is the feeling of hesitation arising in your mind. It usually appears as ~ㄹ지 고민돼요 when a choice is hard. For plain worry, 걱정되다 is more natural.

en: to handle; to deal with; to manage

examples.en: When a problem comes up, you have to deal with it calmly.
I learned how to deal with earthquakes.

examples.ko: 그 직원은 손님의 불만에 잘 대처했어요.
examples.en: The employee handled the customer's complaint well.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 상황에 어떻게 대처할지 생각해 봤어요.
examples.en: I thought about how to cope with a sudden situation.

examples.ko: 위기에 잘 대처하면 기회가 생길 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you handle a crisis well, an opportunity may come.
We train every month to be ready for emergencies.

explain: '문제에 대처하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 같이 써요. '를'은 쓰지 않아요. 대상은 문제, 위기, 갑작스러운 상황처럼 어려운 일이에요. 가벼운 일에는 '처리하다'가 어울려요.

phrases.en: Even if a fire starts, you must handle it calmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위기 상황에서 차분하게 행동하라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say you should act calmly in a crisis.

phrases.example: 위험할 때 대처 방법을 알아 두세요.
phrases.en: Learn how to deal with it when it's dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 일을 처리하는 방법을 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun phrase for how to deal with a difficult situation.

phrases.example: 갑자기 비가 와서 제대로 대처하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: It suddenly rained, so I couldn't handle it properly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황에 알맞게 행동하지 못했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you couldn't act properly in the situation.

explain_en: It goes with the particle 에, as in '문제에 대처하다', not 를. The target is a difficult thing like a problem, a crisis, or a sudden situation. For lighter matters, 처리하다 fits better.

t90.ax: I learned how to deal with earthquakes.
